card.summary: The free SteadIP tier supports HTTP and HTTPS only: "Free users get a random subdomain" and "SteadIP focuses on HTTP and HTTPS first". Dedicated IPv4 is paid...

free_tier.stated: The free SteadIP tier supports HTTP and HTTPS only: "Free users get a random subdomain" and "SteadIP focuses on HTTP and HTTPS first". Dedicated IPv4 is paid: "$29.99 USD per dedicated IPv4 address, billed annually."

egress.terms: No transfer allowance and no fair-use figure are published in the announcement, the product explainer or the homepage. The plan is priced per address per year only.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.interface_detail: Config file plus a customer panel for ports and an optional hostname.
record.tooling: wg-quick; an optional hostname under steadip.com
record.chaining: Pairs with the vendor's own free HTTP tunnel: one address for raw TCP and UDP, one hostname for the website.
record.binding_note: Nothing published fails at 1 TiB/month except an unknown volume policy, so the honest answer is that the wall is undocumented. At USD 29.99 per year for a whole IPv4 the price is not the wall.

identity_cost.detail: A SteadIP account plus a paid annual add-on; the site sells a separate "Verified" tier at USD 19.99 per year, which suggests verification is a paid product rather than an identity check. The signup form was not read.

record.reliability_note: Nothing published on throttling, bans or drop behaviour; the free HTTP tier and the paid Anchor product share a vendor whose main product is an frp-based tunnel.
record.confidence_note: Price, the config file and both inbound modes are first-party. Two gaps: which mode the Anchor add-on includes, and any volume figure. A support question would close both.

evidence.proved: USD 29.99 per year per dedicated IPv4, about USD 2.50 per month; the address is assigned to the account rather than shared
WireGuard config supplied by the vendor; Starter forwards selected ports, Pro and Business offer 1:1 NAT for all ports
the free tier is HTTP and HTTPS with a random subdomain; the paid tunnel tier is USD 19.99 per year

record.price_per_tb_month: USD 29.99 per year per dedicated IPv4 (about USD 2.50 per month)
record.notes: Cheapest whole IPv4 found at USD 29.99 per year, and the only one whose free tier is honestly HTTP-only rather than an IPv6 substitute. Which inbound mode the Anchor add-on gets is not stated, and that decides whether every port is open or a few are forwarded.

extras.wg_detail: "We provide a WireGuard config. You import it on a router, server, VM, or even a desktop." Inbound is either selected ports or all of them: "Port forwarding: forward only the ports you want" or "Forward all ports (1:1 NAT): true full inbound reachability (all ports)".
extras.volume_stated: No transfer allowance and no fair-use figure are published in the announcement, the product explainer or the homepage. The plan is priced per address per year only.
extras.transit_note: The vendor's gateway carries the address and terminates the tunnel; the local ISP only sees outbound.

card.summary: Free HTTP/HTTPS tunnels. Verified features for $19.99 USD/year.

free_tier.stated: Free HTTP/HTTPS tunnels. Verified features for $19.99 USD/year.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published for either tier. The free tier is described as random subdomains over HTTP/HTTPS.; ingress: http-only

record.interface_detail: steadip login then steadip up, configured through the dashboard.
record.tooling: curl -fsSL https://steadip.com/install-linux.sh | sh; steadip login; steadip up.
record.chaining: Free tier fronts a web app on a free VM; UDP needs the paid verified tier, at which point a cheap VPS with frp is comparable in cost.

limits.value: TCP and UDP tunnels require the verified tier at USD 19.99/year

record.binding_note: A verification step and a payment stand between an account and a UDP port, so nothing about volume matters until that gate is passed.

identity_cost.detail: The client command is steadip login against a free account; the TCP/UDP page says the managed layer is available to verified users, and the site prices verified features at USD 19.99 per year.

record.reliability_note: Managed FRP instance shared across customers.
record.confidence_note: Reading the pricing page failed twice (504, then a page with no numbers); a checkout walk would establish the verified tier's actual byte allowance.

evidence.proved: Free HTTP/HTTPS tunnels; verified features for $19.99 USD/year; free users get a random subdomain.
Managed FRP gateway with TCP and UDP options, available to verified users; examples include SSH, game and voice services and UDP telemetry.

record.notes: SteadIP requires paid subscription verification before activating TCP and UDP port forwarding.

extras.wg_detail: The managed gateway is FRP-based and the page says frp supports TCP and UDP proxy types, with TCP and UDP options selectable, but only for verified users. On the free tier there is no UDP listener.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published for either tier. The free tier is described as random subdomains over HTTP/HTTPS.
extras.transit_note: A SteadIP-managed FRP gateway receives public traffic and forwards it down the outbound tunnel.
